A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AC3D and provide readable main text, equations, Figures 1–11, Tables 1–2, and Appendices A–J. The appendix pagination shifts, but no material is missing.

before.justification: v3 reports original quantitative evaluations, ablations, and user-study results in Tables 1–2, alongside motion analysis, camera-pose probing, and CogVideoX experiments.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experimental results, including the quantitative comparisons, user study, and analyses in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The VDiT/VDiT-CC architecture, truncated conditioning schedule, restriction to eight blocks, separate guidance, feedback mechanism, and camera-scaling procedure are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same pretraining data, RealEstate10K and MSR-VTT coverage, curated 20K dynamic-video dataset, and camera-control and pose-probing tasks.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains MotionCtrl and CameraCtrl with U-Net and VDiT backbones, and VD3D with FIT, CogVideoX, and VDiT. Table 1 retains both VD3D comparisons. Newly cited SynCamMaster and ReCamMaster are not evaluated.

E3.justification: Evaluation metrics and settings are unchanged, including the 900/100 probing split, 200-video motion analysis, training budgets, and user study with 10 labelers evaluating 100 pairs each.

E4.justification: Table 2 retains the same ablations of conditioning, noise schedules, guidance, training data, scaling, context, and layer selection. The motion analyses, linear probing, and CogVideoX supplementary analyses also match.

E5.justification: Section 3.3 retains the same 95% confidence-interval reporting, and the plotted uncertainty is unchanged. No run-count, seed, or statistical-testing information is added or revised.

E6.justification: All entries in Tables 1–2 match. For example, AC3D (VDiT) retains FVD values of 36.55 on RealEstate10K and 110.71 on MSR-VTT, while overall user preferences remain 95.0% and 92.5% against VD3D (FIT) and VD3D (DiT). The analysis plots also match.

T1.justification: Equation (1)'s guidance formulation and Appendix H's camera-rescaling optimization are unchanged. No mathematical definitions, assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about camera-motion frequency, internal pose knowledge, conditioning efficiency, scene dynamics, and state-of-the-art camera control.

C2.justification: The mechanism explanations and result interpretations are unchanged. Appendix B retains the same limitations concerning unfamiliar trajectories, latent-space optical-flow analysis, and architecture-specific linear probing.

D1.justification: Appendices D–H preserve the same implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, data processing, dataset construction, and scaling instructions. Project-access information is also unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds SynCamMaster and ReCamMaster as concurrent transformer-based camera-control work using scaled synthetic multiview data, with two corresponding references. This modestly extends related-work coverage without redefining AC3D's positioning.

P1.justification: The prose addition is limited to one sentence in Section 2. The arXiv version/date and CAT4D's bibliography entry are updated, while the remaining narrative and section organization are preserved.

P2.justification: Local text reflow moves the end of Section 3.1 onto page 4, and the final bibliography entry spills onto a nearly empty page 16. Figures and tables retain their content and design; the appendices consequently start one page later.

improvement.justification: Acknowledging SynCamMaster and ReCamMaster modestly improves coverage of directly relevant concurrent research. The scientific evidence, methods, and limitations remain unchanged, so the benefit is confined to contextual completeness; the bibliography spillover is a small layout drawback.
